mechanism_narrative: The recent dip in RETAIL_REC mobility at t-0w, following a period of slight recovery, indicates a reversal of positive momentum, leading to lower retail and recreation mobility over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days, contradicting the recent downward trend.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp week-on-week recovery in WORKPLACES mobility, exceeding a 10 percentage point increase, signals a return to office-based routines that will directly boost associated retail and recreation activities within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises by more than 10 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within two weeks following a week-on-week WORKPLACES increase of more than 10 points.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained elevated RESIDENTIAL mobility combined with GROCERY_PHARM returning to baseline suggests a preference for local, essential activities and home-based leisure, diverting discretionary spending away from broader retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days, despite sustained high RESIDENTIAL and baseline GROCERY_PHARM.

mechanism_narrative: In a context of stable or easing restrictions, a week-on-week recovery in TRANSIT station usage from its recent low indicates increased general movement across the city, which will translate to higher RETAIL_REC within four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next four weeks when TRANSIT shows a week-on-week rise under easing restrictions.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in PARKS mobility, falling below -20% from baseline, indicates a general reduction in outdoor leisure activities and increased time spent indoors, which will negatively impact RETAIL_REC within one week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases within one week after PARKS mobility drops below -20% from baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous sharp recovery in WORKPLACES mobility and a decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility signals a strong shift back to pre-pandemic commuting and work patterns, which will drive an increase in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises week-on-week AND RESIDENTIAL falls week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 28 days when WORKPLACES rises and RESIDENTIAL falls week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: The recent stabilization of GROCERY_PHARM mobility around baseline indicates that essential needs are consistently met, but without a broader surge in activity, discretionary retail will remain subdued, leading to continued low RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is significantly higher than over the last 28 days, despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining stable around baseline.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime of tightening restrictions, any temporary increases in TRANSIT or WORKPLACES mobility are quickly reversed due to policy enforcement or public caution, leading to a sustained decline in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days despite tightening restrictions and initial increases in TRANSIT or WORKPLACES being reversed.
